* perf(AUTO-1063): skip parsing hostnames and cache verdicts in isAddressRestricted

A hostname made ipaddr.process() throw on every request (~7 us for the
stack trace), and an IPv4 address threw once per IPv6 range in the
policy. Return early for hosts that cannot be an IP literal, and
remember verdicts per host string on networkOptions.restrictedVerdicts
(bounded at 1,000 entries). Verdicts are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(AUTO-1063): evict least recently used isAddressRestricted verdict instead of clearing the cache

Refresh recency on a hit and evict the oldest entry on overflow, so frequently used verdicts survive when the cache fills.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(AUTO-1063): assert isAddressRestricted pre-check covers every IPv4 form ipaddr.js accepts

Generated-corpus property test: every colon-free string ipaddr.js
accepts must reach the parser, so an ipaddr.js bump that widens its
IPv4 grammar (e.g. 0o octal) fails CI instead of opening a bypass.
Also corrects the pre-check and verdict-cache comments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(AUTO-1063): skip parsing hostnames and cache verdicts in isAddressRestricted (#1571)

* perf(AUTO-1063): skip parsing hostnames and cache verdicts in isAddressRestricted

A hostname made ipaddr.process() throw on every request (~7 us for the
stack trace), and an IPv4 address threw once per IPv6 range in the
policy. Return early for hosts that cannot be an IP literal, and
remember verdicts per host string on networkOptions.restrictedVerdicts
(bounded at 1,000 entries). Verdicts are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(AUTO-1063): evict least recently used isAddressRestricted verdict instead of clearing the cache

Refresh recency on a hit and evict the oldest entry on overflow, so frequently used verdicts survive when the cache fills.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(AUTO-1063): assert isAddressRestricted pre-check covers every IPv4 form ipaddr.js accepts

Generated-corpus property test: every colon-free string ipaddr.js
accepts must reach the parser, so an ipaddr.js bump that widens its
IPv4 grammar (e.g. 0o octal) fails CI instead of opening a bypass.
Also corrects the pre-check and verdict-cache comments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
